text: How do you share operational data with partner agencies, governments, and coordination clusters?

options.text: Our organization operates independently without formal participation in regional inter-agency meetings.
Staff attends regional coordination cluster meetings and shares meeting notes internally via email.
Operational summaries are formatted into standard 3W/4W (Who, What, Where, When) templates and submitted to coordination leads on schedule.
Automated data pipelines stream anonymized distribution and coverage metrics directly into open humanitarian data exchanges (e.g., HDX).

text: How do you collect community feedback and handle grievances from affected populations?

options.text: Feedback is collected informally only when community members approach field staff with complaints.
Physical suggestion boxes are placed at distribution points and checked periodically by staff.
Dedicated monitoring teams conduct post-distribution mobile surveys with randomized beneficiary samples 30 days after aid delivery.
A multi-channel accountability platform (toll-free hotlines, SMS, messaging apps) logs complaints with automated escalation protocols and trackable resolution timelines.

text: How do you assess community needs and damage during the onset of an emergency or disaster?

options.text: Field staff conducts informal visual site visits and writes summaries after returning to headquarters.
Assessment teams fill out digital forms or spreadsheets on laptops and email them when an internet connection is available.
Mobile data collection tools (e.g., KoboToolbox, ODK) capture GPS-tagged survey responses with offline data caching.
An integrated spatial assessment platform combines mobile surveyor inputs, satellite/drone mapping, and predictive needs modeling in real time.

text: How are relief supplies, emergency kits, and food rations managed in storage hubs?

options.text: Supplies and emergency kits are stored in general facilities without structured bin locations or lot tracking.
Staff updates incoming donations and outgoing shipments weekly using shared spreadsheets.
A centralized inventory database tracks non-food item (NFI) stock levels, batch numbers, and expiration dates.
A multi-echelon humanitarian logistics platform tracks pre-positioned stock globally, triggering automated replenishment based on field depletion rates.

text: How do you manage spontaneous and registered volunteers during emergency operations?

options.text: Volunteers deploy informally to distribution sites and check in on paper sign-up clipboards.
Coordinators use spreadsheets to schedule volunteer shifts and communicate updates through broadcast text messages.
A digital volunteer management portal manages online onboarding, safety liability waivers, and shift scheduling.
An emergency deployment app matches volunteer skills to urgent needs, tracks real-time on-site check-ins, and manages emergency SOS safety check-ins.

text: How do you maintain the cold chain for temperature-sensitive medical supplies and vaccines?

options.text: Vaccines and medicines are packed in standard insulated coolers with ice packs without temperature logging.
Staff checks manual thermometers at origin departure and final destination arrival only.
Digital data loggers placed inside transport containers record temperatures throughout transit for review upon receipt.
Solar-powered IoT cold-chain units stream real-time temperature, humidity, and location telemetry via satellite, alerting teams to excursions immediately.

text: How do you verify beneficiaries and manage distribution queues in the field?

options.text: Beneficiaries sign physical paper rosters or provide a signature/thumbprint on printed sheets.
Field workers issue paper ration cards printed with barcodes and scan them at distribution tables.
A mobile beneficiary management app checks photo IDs or tokens against a centralized registration database.
Biometric or smart-card verification systems prevent duplicate rations in real time, synchronizing offline distribution records upon reconnection.

text: How are cash transfers and voucher assistance (CVA) programs delivered to recipients?

options.text: Physical cash envelopes are handed directly to recipients against signed paper payment receipts.
Paper vouchers are distributed for redemption at approved local merchants, with staff reimbursing merchants manually.
Pre-loaded debit or stored-value cards are distributed and topped up through scheduled batch bank transfers.
Digital mobile-money wallets and secure digital voucher platforms enable instant disbursement, automated fraud checks, and real-time merchant reconciliation.

text: How do you track and maintain your relief vehicle fleet and transport operations?

options.text: Drivers operate vehicles without structured logbooks, and maintenance is addressed only after a breakdown occurs.
Paper trip logs and fuel purchase receipts are reconciled manually at the end of each month.
Fleet management software tracks preventive maintenance schedules, fuel consumption trends, and driver assignments.
Satellite-linked telematics track convoy movements in real time with geofencing, driver safety monitoring, and dynamic conflict-zone rerouting.

text: How does your team release new features and software updates?

options.text: We manually copy-paste or upload files directly to the live server.
A developer manually runs update scripts on the server.
We use an automated CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment) pipeline that tests code before deploying.
Our updates are fully automated across multiple regions with zero downtime, gradual canary rollouts, and instant rollbacks.

text: What happens to your system when user traffic suddenly spikes?

options.text: The website or app slows down or crashes; we have to restart the server manually.
We manually upgrade server power (CPU / RAM) when we expect a rush.
Our cloud servers automatically add more instances based on set CPU and memory limits.
We use containerized, cloud-native architecture (such as Kubernetes or Serverless) that auto-scales instantly based on live traffic.

text: How do you find out about technical bugs, crashes, or slow performance?

options.text: We only find out when customers contact support or complain on social media.
Our engineers manually log in and review error log files after an issue is reported.
We use centralized APM (Application Performance Monitoring) tools with automated email/Slack alerts for critical errors.
We have live distributed tracing and observability dashboards that detect and isolate errors before users notice.

text: How do you track if customers are happy or about to stop using your product?

options.text: We only know a customer is leaving after they cancel their plan or stop paying.
We manually check account login dates at the end of each month.
We track in-app health scores based on login frequency and core feature usage.
The system uses automated behavioral tracking to spot drop-off signs early and trigger automated re-engagement messages.

text: What is the welcome and setup process for a new customer?

options.text: Users land on an empty dashboard with no guidance, or receive a basic PDF (Portable Document Format) guide.
We send a standard automated welcome email with links to our help center.
We provide interactive in-app setup checklists and product walkthrough tours.
We provide personalized setup journeys based on user roles, complete with milestone tracking and automated check-ins.

text: How easily can external software or partner apps connect to your product?

options.text: We do not offer APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) or third-party integrations.
We share custom integration links on a case-by-case basis with manual instructions.
We offer standardized, documented REST (Representational State Transfer) or GraphQL (Graph Query Language) APIs with secure access key management.
We provide a self-service developer portal with instant API keys, interactive sandboxes, webhooks, and pre-built SDKs (Software Development Kits).

text: How do you check for security flaws and software vulnerabilities?

options.text: We only address security issues if an incident or data breach occurs.
We run occasional manual security reviews or periodic annual audits.
Automated vulnerability and code quality scans run on every pull request before code is merged.
We run continuous automated testing (SAST / DAST), routine dependency patching, and regular penetration testing.

text: What happens if your main database crashes completely?

options.text: We rely on occasional manual backups; a crash would cause significant, permanent data loss.
We have daily automated backups, but restoring them has not been recently tested.
We run automated daily off-site backups with documented recovery targets — RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective).
We have live multi-region data replication with automated failover and zero data loss architecture.

text: How does your team track how people actually use your platform?

options.text: We rely on basic website page views and total visitor counts.
We only track basic conversion steps (e.g., website visit to account creation).
We use event-based analytics tools to track user journeys, feature adoption, and retention cohorts.
We run a unified CDP (Customer Data Platform) that connects in-app behavior directly to personalized features, messaging, and experimentation.

text: How do you verify customer identity during sign-up?

options.text: We collect and check physical paper ID photocopies by hand.
Customers upload document photos, and our team checks them manually.
Software automatically checks IDs and live photos using digital KYC (Know Your Customer).
Verification is 100% instant and automatic using e-KYC (electronic Know Your Customer) and anti-crime database checks.

text: How do you match and balance daily transactions across bank accounts?

options.text: We manually check numbers on paper bank statements or Excel sheets at month-end.
We manually match bank statements in Excel once a week.
Software automatically matches bank statements daily and flags payment differences.
Our system matches and balances all transactions across all banks instantly in real time.

text: How do you detect and stop fraudulent payments?

options.text: We only find out after a customer complains or a bank alerts us.
Our staff manually reviews high-value or suspicious transactions one by one.
Basic software rules automatically block suspicious payments (e.g., wrong country or repeated failed attempts).
Smart AI (Artificial Intelligence) instantly scores payment risk in milliseconds and blocks fraud before money leaves.

text: How do you protect customer bank details and card numbers?

options.text: Details are saved in regular files or spreadsheets without password protection or encryption.
Basic database security is turned on, but passwords and permissions are managed manually.
We follow standard card security rules (PCI-DSS) and mask card numbers so raw data is never saved.
We use high-grade bank-level security hardware (HSM) and strict data locks with annual security audits.

glossary.fullForm: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard

text: How do you check and approve loan or credit applications?

options.text: Loan officers manually read paper forms, salary slips, and physical signatures.
We manually check online credit scores (like CIBIL) and calculate eligibility in Excel.
Software automatically fetches credit bureau scores and gives quick approvals.
The system checks live bank statements and cash flows to approve and disburse loans instantly.

text: How do you prepare and file government/regulatory compliance reports?

options.text: We manually create reports in Excel when regulators or auditors ask for them.
We run database reports and format the numbers by hand to file them.
Specialized software automatically generates monthly filings and suspicious activity logs.
Automated compliance tools (RegTech) track rules 24/7 and file reports directly to regulators without manual effort.

text: How do partner businesses and apps connect to your software?

options.text: Partners must email data files or send spreadsheets manually.
We create custom connection links and manual setup guides when requested.
We provide standard, secure connection links (APIs) with a test area.
We offer a self-service developer portal where partners can connect and go live instantly.

text: What happens when a payment fails or a customer disputes a charge?

options.text: Customers must submit physical forms or call; fixing the issue takes weeks.
Support staff manually emails the payment gateway or bank to trace the issue.
An in-app dispute button sends the issue straight into our support system with fixed turnaround times.
The system retries failed payments automatically and resolves disputes with banks with zero human effort.

text: How do you track and manage overall cash flow and bank balances?

options.text: We log in and check separate bank account balances once a week or month.
The finance team checks all bank balances and makes an Excel summary every morning.
We use a single dashboard that shows daily total balances and pending payouts.
An automated treasury system tracks live cash across all banks, predicts future cash needs, and moves funds automatically.

text: How do you track stock levels and material locations in your godown or warehouse?

options.text: Workers rely on paper registers, whiteboards, or memory to find and count items.
We enter stock quantities in Excel or simple billing software and update rack locations by hand.
We use dedicated WMS (Warehouse Management System) software with barcode scanners to track shelf bins and stock in real time.
Our warehouse uses RFID (Radio-Frequency Identification) tags and smart systems to locate and move stock automatically.

text: How does your godown team pick and pack goods for dispatch?

options.text: Helpers walk around with printed delivery challans or kachha slips, packing one order at a time.
The godown supervisor groups orders manually on an Excel sheet and gives printed picking lists to workers.
Software groups orders automatically and guides helpers along the fastest walking path using barcode scanners.
We use automated conveyor systems and electronic weight-check packing tables to pack orders with zero manual error.

text: How do you book trucks, tempos, and transport companies for your dispatches?

options.text: We call local transport brokers or Transport Nagar agents daily on the phone to negotiate market spot rates.
We maintain fixed transporter rate cards in Excel and book dispatches by calling or using individual courier websites.
A TMS (Transportation Management System) automatically assigns loads to approved transporters based on lowest cost and committed delivery times.
Our system connects directly via APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) to online freight platforms for instant truck booking and live market bidding.

text: How do you track the live transit location and delivery status of your goods?

options.text: We call the truck driver or transport broker on mobile to ask where the vehicle has reached.
Staff manually opens transporter tracking websites, copies the status, and updates clients over WhatsApp or email.
Transporter systems send automated status updates directly to our software, triggering alerts if a shipment is delayed.
We use live GPS (Global Positioning System) vehicle trackers and IoT (Internet of Things) sensors to get real-time ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) updates.

text: How do you decide when to reorder raw materials or finished goods?

options.text: We place purchase orders only after godown workers notice that stocks or bins are running out.
We manually calculate reorder quantities in Excel once a month based on past sales averages.
Our ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) software automatically calculates safety stock levels and creates purchase orders based on seasonal demand.
Smart AI (Artificial Intelligence) software tracks live market sales, supplier delivery delays, and factory capacity to automate purchase orders.

text: How do you plan local and last-mile delivery routes for your drivers?

options.text: Drivers look at address slips or invoices and decide their own driving routes based on their personal memory.
Dispatchers divide deliveries into fixed geographic areas and assign fixed delivery days for each zone.
Route-planning software creates daily optimized vehicle delivery routes to reduce fuel costs and travel time.
Software recalculates delivery routes in real time based on live traffic jams and sends live SMS (Short Message Service) tracking links to buyers.

text: How do you monitor temperature for sensitive or cold-chain items (like pharma, food, or dairy)?

options.text: Drivers check manual dial thermometers only during truck loading and final unloading.
We put simple digital temperature data-loggers inside boxes and download the readings after delivery is complete.
Refrigerated vehicles (Reefer trucks) have digital sensors that sound an alarm if the compartment temperature crosses safe limits.
Wireless IoT sensors stream live temperature and humidity to a cloud dashboard 24/7, sending instant mobile alerts if cooling drops.

text: How does your facility process customer returns and damaged goods?

options.text: Returned stock is dumped in a corner of the godown and checked only when staff has free time.
Staff checks returns against physical paper bills, updates stock in Excel, and raises credit notes by hand.
A standard RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) process uses barcode scanning to sort returns into restock, repair, or scrap bins.
Automated return stations inspect and grade returned items immediately, restocking good units and issuing digital credit notes automatically.

text: How do you audit transporter freight bills and clear payments?

options.text: Accounts clears transport bills against purchase orders directly without checking weight or trip charges line-by-line.
Accounts staff manually matches paper transport bills against original quotation slips and delivery challans.
Automated software verifies transport bills against agreed freight rate cards and signed LR (Lorry Receipt) / POD (Proof of Delivery) copies.
An automated system checks freight invoices digitally, flags incorrect weight or detention charges instantly, and clears verified payments through the ERP.

text: How do you assign team members to client projects and manage their workload?

options.text: Project leads book consultants informally through personal phone calls or WhatsApp messages.
Partner and manager teams review team availability once a week using a shared Excel sheet.
A centralized resource planning tool tracks each consultant's skills, ongoing client commitments, and future availability.
Smart software automatically matches consultant skills, career goals, and profit margin targets to project requirements.

text: How do your consultants log daily work hours and track billable time?

options.text: Team members guess hours from memory at the end of the month and email Excel timesheets to accounts.
Staff fills out weekly digital timesheets that project managers check and approve manually.
A PSA (Professional Services Automation) tool tracks daily billable vs. non-billable hours against project codes.
Automated software tracks calendar meetings and document work in the background, showing live staff utilization and budget burn-rate alerts.

text: How do you track project scope, milestones, and deliverable deadlines?

options.text: Deliverables and deadlines are agreed informally over email, and extra client requests are handled without formal pricing changes.
Project managers track task schedules in Excel and manually prepare written change requests when scope increases.
Dedicated project software tracks task dependencies, deliverable dates, and budget spending against the signed SOW (Statement of Work).
Delivery tracking software analyzes daily completion speed to alert leadership about deadline risks and profit margin drops weeks in advance.

text: How does your firm save and reuse past project reports, templates, and frameworks?

options.text: Past presentations, proposals, and deliverables remain saved on individual consultants' personal laptops.
Staff searches through unorganized Google Drive or shared folders to find old templates.
A central digital knowledge base organizes standard project frameworks, proposal templates, and industry benchmarks.
An AI (Artificial Intelligence) search engine indexes all past deliverables, automatically suggesting relevant case studies and drafting new proposals.

text: How are client invoices prepared, sent, and matched with completed work?

options.text: Accounts types Word document invoices manually weeks after project work or milestones are finished.
Finance enters billable hours from timesheets into basic accounting software (like Tally) at month-end.
Invoices are generated automatically from approved PSA timesheets, expenses, and fixed-fee milestone sign-offs.
Automated billing software tracks real-time WIP (Work-In-Progress), provides client online approval portals, and manages digital payment collections.

text: How do you prepare proposals, pitch presentations, and tender responses for new clients?

options.text: Every client pitch or proposal is created from scratch in PowerPoint with rough pricing estimates.
Team members copy-paste content and slides from previous successful client decks saved on their systems.
Proposal software provides a centralized library of approved case studies, team bios, standardized rate cards, and legal terms.
A smart proposal platform analyzes past win-loss data to recommend the most profitable project team structure, pricing, and custom content.

text: How do you onboard new clients and execute legal contracts, service agreements, and confidentiality agreements?

options.text: Standard contracts are printed on letterhead/stamp paper, signed by hand, scanned, and emailed back and forth.
Contract PDFs (Portable Document Formats) are sent using basic e-signature tools, with dates tracked manually.
Automated digital workflows handle standard NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement) and MSA (Master Services Agreement) generation, digital signing, and client project setup.
A fully automated onboarding portal manages contract signing, conflict-of-interest checks, team access permissions, and billing setup with zero manual delay.

text: How do you collect client feedback and measure satisfaction during and after a project?

options.text: Feedback is collected informally only when a client is unhappy, complains, or threatens to hold payments.
Senior partners make informal phone calls to the client sponsor after the project is completed.
Automated NPS (Net Promoter Score) and CSAT (Customer Satisfaction) surveys are sent to key client stakeholders at set project milestones.
A real-time client feedback platform tracks survey scores, email communication speed, and milestone approvals to give a live account health score.

text: How do you manage freelance consultants, subject matter experts, and partner agencies?

options.text: Freelancers and external experts are hired through verbal agreements with variable, ad-hoc payment terms.
Contractor contact details and rates are kept in an Excel sheet, and bills are collected manually.
A vendor portal tracks contractor compliance, standard hourly rates, signed NDAs, and approved timesheets.
An online talent platform manages automated background verification, skill matching, digital contract onboarding, time tracking, and payouts.

text: How do you update stock availability across your retail shops, website, and marketplaces (like Amazon, Flipkart, or Myntra)?

options.text: We track stock in separate, disconnected registers or software for each shop and sales channel.
Staff manually updates stock quantities between store billing software and our website once or twice a day in Excel.
A centralized inventory system automatically updates stock levels across all online and offline channels on a fixed schedule.
A real-time DOM (Distributed Order Management) system maintains a single shared stock pool, automatically dispatching orders from the nearest shop or godown.

text: How do you manage product descriptions, photos, and size charts across all selling platforms?

options.text: Product details and photos are stored in basic folders and Excel sheets, and uploaded to each channel by hand.
Shop staff and digital marketing teams create product listings separately in store billing and website portals.
A dedicated PIM (Product Information Management) system sends standardized product catalogs, images, and prices to all channels.
An automated PIM system uses AI (Artificial Intelligence) to write product copy, optimize SEO (Search Engine Optimization) tags, and publish listings to marketplaces instantly.

text: How do you manage product selling prices, festive discounts, and promotional offers?

options.text: Prices and discounts are changed manually on each website channel and by reprinting paper price tags in physical stores.
Marketing staff sets up promo coupon codes separately in store billing software and on the e-commerce website.
A central pricing engine applies scheduled discount rules, seasonal sale prices, and regional pricing across all billing points automatically.
Smart pricing algorithms track competitor pricing on marketplaces and stock clearance speeds to adjust prices automatically in real time.

text: What payment options do online customers see during checkout on your website or app?

options.text: A basic multi-step checkout page that only accepts standard debit/credit card details.
A checkout page supporting cards, Net Banking, and basic COD (Cash On Delivery) verification.
A quick one-page checkout offering UPI (Unified Payments Interface), digital wallets (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm), and BNPL (Buy Now Pay Later) options.
A seamless one-click checkout with automatic UPI intent routing, automated COD-to-prepaid conversion prompts, and instant payment fraud checks.

text: How do you run customer loyalty programs and encourage repeat purchases?

options.text: We use physical paper stamp cards or do not have any formal customer loyalty system.
Cashiers collect customer mobile numbers and email IDs at billing to send occasional WhatsApp/SMS festive greetings.
An integrated loyalty software tracks reward points across both physical store billing counters and online website orders.
A personalized customer retention system sends automated, customized discount vouchers and product suggestions based on past buying history.

text: How do your physical retail stores help fulfill online website or app orders?

options.text: Retail stores do not handle web orders; all online deliveries ship only from a central main godown.
Store staff prints online order slips when free, manually packing items from shop shelves without special tools.
Store staff uses a mobile app to pick and pack orders for customer store pickups — BOPIS (Buy Online, Pick Up In Store) or local parcel handover.
The system routes online orders automatically to the nearest store with available stock for same-day local delivery via bike couriers (e.g., Dunzo, Porter, Shadowfax).
